state.name: Pennsylvania
state.peak_intrusion_season: March through May during spring raccoon and squirrel denning and groundhog emergence, summer for bat maternity colonies under Game Commission guidance and peak mole and groundhog lawn damage, and late September through November as squirrels and rodents seek winter shelter
state.climate_factor: Pennsylvania's four full seasons — cold winters and hot, humid summers — push squirrels, rodents, and overwintering big brown bats into attics in winter while keeping raccoons, skunks, and groundhogs active in yards from early spring through late fall
state.permit_note: Pennsylvania requires anyone doing commercial nuisance wildlife work for another person to hold a Pennsylvania Game Commission nuisance wildlife control operator permit under 58 Pa. Code Chapter 147, Subchapter T; captured rabies-vector species — raccoons, skunks, foxes, coyotes, bats, and groundhogs — are never released, and other captured wildlife is euthanized humanely or released only in an area open to hunting or trapping within 24 hours under 58 Pa. Code Section 147.726(g)

Philadelphia County.region: southeastern Pennsylvania on the Delaware River, consolidated city-county at the heart of the Delaware Valley
Philadelphia County.nearest_metro: Philadelphia is itself the metro center and Pennsylvania's largest city
Philadelphia County.habitat_type: dense urban row-home neighborhoods, brick twins, and older apartment blocks threaded by wooded river park corridors
Philadelphia County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats are entrenched in the older row-home blocks, alleys, and sewer lines from South Philadelphia to Kensington, raccoons den in chimneys and rooflines across the Northeast and Northwest, and the Wissahickon and Fairmount Park corridors carry squirrels, skunks, and opossums deep into residential streets
Philadelphia County.absent_or_rare: white-tailed deer, foxes, and coyotes live along the park corridors but are managed by the Pennsylvania Game Commission rather than handled as routine household removal work

Delaware County.region: southeastern Pennsylvania between Philadelphia and the Delaware state line, in the inner Delaware Valley suburbs
Delaware County.nearest_metro: Philadelphia (the county borders the city to the northeast)
Delaware County.habitat_type: dense inner suburbs of brick twins, rowhouses, and postwar singles over older borough cores
Delaware County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and squirrels work the mature street trees and older rooflines of Upper Darby, Drexel Hill, and Havertown, Norway rats hold the older commercial blocks and waterfront industry in Chester, and Ridley Creek and Darby Creek feed skunks, opossums, and groundhogs into yards across Springfield and Marple
Delaware County.absent_or_rare: black bears and bobcats are not established in this urban county, and white-tailed deer along the creek parks fall under Pennsylvania Game Commission management rather than private removal

Chester County.region: southeastern Pennsylvania, the western edge of the Philadelphia suburbs giving way to farm country
Chester County.nearest_metro: Philadelphia (about 25 miles east of West Chester)
natural_features: ChesLen Preserve and White Clay Creek
Chester County.habitat_type: fast-growing suburbs in the east, historic boroughs along the Brandywine, and working farms and mushroom country in the south
Chester County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs burrow fence lines and barn edges from Kennett Square to Honey Brook, raccoons and gray squirrels fill the attics of West Chester, Downingtown, and the Main Line edge, and Brandywine Creek bottomland carries skunks and opossums into borough back yards
Chester County.absent_or_rare: black bears pass through the northern townships only rarely, and beavers and white-tailed deer along the creeks are Pennsylvania Game Commission matters rather than routine removal calls

Montgomery County.region: southeastern Pennsylvania, the northwestern Philadelphia suburbs along the Schuylkill River
Montgomery County.nearest_metro: Philadelphia (the county touches the city along its southeastern edge)
natural_features: Perkiomen Creek and Green Lane Park
Montgomery County.habitat_type: dense suburbs and Main Line communities in the south and east, older river boroughs, and rural townships in the northwest
Montgomery County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and squirrels are constant in the mature-canopy suburbs from Ardmore to Abington, Norway rats persist in Norristown and Pottstown's older blocks, and groundhogs and moles work the lawns and farm edges from Green Lane to the Perkiomen valley
Montgomery County.absent_or_rare: black bears are only occasional visitors to the northwestern townships, and deer, beavers, and foxes along the Schuylkill and Perkiomen are managed by the Pennsylvania Game Commission

Bucks County.region: southeastern Pennsylvania along the Delaware River, the northern tier of the Philadelphia suburbs
natural_features: Delaware River and Delaware Canal corridor
Lake Nockamixon and Nockamixon State Park
Bucks County.habitat_type: postwar Levittown-era suburbs in the south, historic boroughs and horse farms in the center, and wooded river hills in the north
Bucks County.regional_wildlife: gray squirrels and raccoons dominate calls from Levittown and Bensalem to Doylestown, groundhogs burrow the farm and large-lot edges of central Bucks, and the Neshaminy and Delaware corridors move skunks and opossums through Newtown, Warminster, and the river towns
Bucks County.absent_or_rare: black bears appear in upper Bucks only as wanderers, and beavers, deer, and Canada geese on the river and lakes fall under Pennsylvania Game Commission and federal rules rather than private removal

Lancaster County.region: south-central Pennsylvania, Pennsylvania Dutch farm country between the Susquehanna River and the Philadelphia suburbs
Lancaster County.nearest_metro: Harrisburg (about 35 miles northwest) and Philadelphia (about 70 miles east)
natural_features: Welsh Mountain and Speedwell Forge Lake
Lancaster County.habitat_type: some of the most productive farmland in the East, with dense boroughs, Plain Sect farmsteads, and fast-growing suburbs
Lancaster County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs are a daily fact of farm life along fence rows and bank barns countywide, raccoons raid feed rooms and den in Lancaster city and borough attics, and big brown bats hold old colonies in the stone farmhouses and tobacco barns of the Conestoga valley
Lancaster County.absent_or_rare: black bears are rare wanderers this far into farm country, and white-tailed deer and beavers are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed species rather than household removal work

Berks County.region: southeastern Pennsylvania in the Schuylkill River valley between the Philadelphia suburbs and the Blue Mountain ridge
Berks County.nearest_metro: Reading is the regional center, with Philadelphia about 55 miles southeast
natural_features: Blue Mountain and Hawk Mountain Sanctuary
Antietam Lake and French Creek State Park edge
Tulpehocken Creek and Blue Marsh Lake
Berks County.habitat_type: the older industrial city of Reading, streetcar suburbs, and broad farm valleys under the Blue Mountain ridge
Berks County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats persist in Reading's older row-home and warehouse blocks, raccoons and squirrels work Wyomissing and the boroughs along the Schuylkill, and groundhogs and skunks fill the farm edges from Kutztown to Hamburg under Blue Mountain
Berks County.absent_or_rare: black bears come down off Blue Mountain into northern townships but are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed, as are deer and beavers along the Tulpehocken

Lehigh County.region: eastern Pennsylvania in the Lehigh Valley along the Lehigh River
Lehigh County.nearest_metro: Allentown is the regional center, about 60 miles north of Philadelphia
natural_features: Lehigh Gap and the Appalachian Trail ridge
Jordan Creek and Little Lehigh Creek
Lehigh County.habitat_type: the industrial city of Allentown, dense boroughs, warehouse-corridor suburbs, and farm townships under South Mountain
Lehigh County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and gray squirrels are heavy across Allentown, Whitehall, and the borough ring, Norway rats hold older commercial and riverfront blocks, and groundhogs and moles work the big suburban lawns and farm edges from Macungie to Coopersburg
Lehigh County.absent_or_rare: black bears wander in from the Blue Mountain ridge only occasionally, and deer, beavers, and foxes are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed rather than private removal work

Northampton County.region: eastern Pennsylvania in the Lehigh Valley where the Lehigh River meets the Delaware River
Northampton County.nearest_metro: Allentown-Bethlehem-Easton is the regional metro, about 70 miles north of Philadelphia
natural_features: Blue Mountain ridge and Appalachian Trail
Northampton County.habitat_type: historic Easton and Bethlehem industrial blocks, slate-belt boroughs in the north, and suburban growth along the river corridors
Northampton County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and squirrels work the older rooflines of Easton, Bethlehem, and the slate-belt boroughs, rats persist around the riverfront and older commercial stock, and groundhogs burrow the farm and quarry edges from Nazareth to Bangor
Northampton County.absent_or_rare: black bears are occasional visitors off Blue Mountain, and deer, beaver, and fisher activity in the northern woods is Pennsylvania Game Commission business rather than routine removal

York County.region: south-central Pennsylvania along the Susquehanna River's west shore, bordering Maryland
York County.nearest_metro: Harrisburg (about 25 miles north) across the Susquehanna
natural_features: Codorus Creek and Lake Marburg at Codorus State Park
Rocky Ridge and Samuel S. Lewis State Park
York County.habitat_type: the older industrial city of York, snack-food and manufacturing boroughs, and rolling farm country to the Maryland line
York County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs burrow farm edges and Hanover-area gardens all season, raccoons and squirrels fill York city and suburban attics, and Norway rats persist in the older industrial blocks of York and Spring Grove
York County.absent_or_rare: black bears are uncommon wanderers from the northern ridges, and deer, beavers, and muskrats along the Susquehanna and Codorus are managed by the Pennsylvania Game Commission

Dauphin County.region: south-central Pennsylvania on the east shore of the Susquehanna River, home to the state capital
Dauphin County.nearest_metro: Harrisburg is the state capital and regional metro center
natural_features: Blue Mountain and Peters Mountain ridges
Wildwood Park and the Harrisburg greenbelt
Dauphin County.habitat_type: the capital city and older river boroughs, Hershey's planned community, and ridge-and-valley suburbs to the north
Dauphin County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and gray squirrels run the mature street trees of Harrisburg, Hershey, and Linglestown, Norway rats hold the older blocks of Steelton and Middletown, and groundhogs work the farm and large-lot edges under Blue Mountain
Dauphin County.absent_or_rare: black bears come down Peters Mountain into the northern townships but are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed, as are deer and beavers on the Swatara

Cumberland County.region: south-central Pennsylvania in the Cumberland Valley on the Susquehanna's west shore
Cumberland County.habitat_type: fast-growing capital suburbs in the east, the historic college town of Carlisle, and farm valley toward Shippensburg
Cumberland County.regional_wildlife: squirrels and raccoons are steady in Camp Hill, Lemoyne, and Mechanicsburg's mature suburbs, groundhogs burrow valley farm edges and new-subdivision lots, and bats roost in Carlisle's older stone and brick housing
Cumberland County.absent_or_rare: black bears are occasional visitors off South Mountain, and deer, beavers, and muskrats along the Conodoguinet fall under Pennsylvania Game Commission management

Lebanon County.region: south-central Pennsylvania in the Lebanon Valley between Harrisburg and Reading
natural_features: Middle Creek Wildlife Management Area southern edge
South Mountain foothills and the old Cornwall iron lands
Lebanon County.habitat_type: a small industrial city, Pennsylvania Dutch farm valley, and commuter suburbs toward Hershey and Harrisburg
Lebanon County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs and skunks work the farm edges and borough yards from Myerstown to Annville, raccoons den in Lebanon city's older homes, and bats use the stone farmhouses and barns along the Swatara
Lebanon County.absent_or_rare: black bears are rare wanderers from South Mountain, and deer, beavers, and wild turkeys in the valley are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed species

Adams County.region: south-central Pennsylvania, Gettysburg battlefield country along the Maryland line
Adams County.nearest_metro: Harrisburg (about 35 miles northeast) and Baltimore (about 55 miles southeast)
Adams County.habitat_type: historic battlefield boroughs, orchard country around Biglerville and Arendtsville, and rural residential growth
Adams County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs burrow orchard edges and battlefield fence lines, raccoons and skunks work Gettysburg's older homes and the boroughs along Route 30, and bats roost in the stone houses and barns of the orchard country
Adams County.absent_or_rare: black bears wander down from Michaux and South Mountain only occasionally, and deer and turkeys on the battlefield are managed by the Pennsylvania Game Commission and the National Park Service

Franklin County.region: south-central Pennsylvania in the Cumberland Valley along the Maryland line
Franklin County.nearest_metro: Hagerstown, Maryland (about 20 miles south of Chambersburg)
Franklin County.habitat_type: valley farm country and warehouse corridor along I-81, with mountain forest on both sides
Franklin County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs burrow farm and orchard edges from Greencastle to Mercersburg, raccoons and squirrels fill Chambersburg and Waynesboro housing, and skunks work the valley floor lawns all summer
Franklin County.absent_or_rare: black bears are regular in the Michaux and Tuscarora forests but are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed, as are deer and beavers along the Conococheague

Luzerne County.region: northeastern Pennsylvania in the Wyoming Valley along the Susquehanna River, historic anthracite coal country
natural_features: Susquehanna River through the Wyoming Valley
Lehigh River gorge at the county's east
Frances Slocum and Ricketts Glen state parks
Luzerne County.habitat_type: dense coal-era cities and boroughs in the valley, mine-scarred hillsides, and mountain suburbs
Luzerne County.regional_wildlife: raccoons, squirrels, and rats run the dense older housing of Wilkes-Barre, Pittston, and Nanticoke, bats colonize coal-era attics and church belfries across the valley, and skunks and groundhogs work the Mountain Top and Hazleton edges
Luzerne County.absent_or_rare: black bears are common in the surrounding mountains but are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed, as are deer, beavers, and fishers in the state parks

Lackawanna County.region: northeastern Pennsylvania in the Lackawanna Valley, the northern half of the Scranton-Wilkes-Barre metro
Lackawanna County.nearest_metro: Scranton is the regional center, about 100 miles north of Philadelphia
natural_features: Moosic Mountain and the Pocono edge
Nay Aug Park gorge in Scranton
Lackawanna County.habitat_type: the dense older city of Scranton, coal-era valley boroughs, and Abington suburbs climbing out of the valley
Lackawanna County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats and raccoons persist in Scranton's older neighborhoods and along the Lackawanna River, squirrels and bats fill Dunmore, Old Forge, and Carbondale housing, and skunks dig lawns across the Abingtons
Lackawanna County.absent_or_rare: black bears are regular visitors off Moosic Mountain but are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed, as are beavers and deer along the Lackawanna River

Monroe County.region: northeastern Pennsylvania in the Poconos along the Delaware River and the New Jersey line
Monroe County.nearest_metro: the Stroudsburgs are the local center, with the New York metro about 75 miles east
natural_features: Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area
Camelback Mountain and Big Pocono State Park
Monroe County.habitat_type: Pocono resort and vacation-home communities, lake developments, and fast-growing commuter suburbs in deep forest
Monroe County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats are the signature problem in vacation and second homes that sit empty between visits, squirrels chew into lake-community houses from Tobyhanna to Brodheadsville, and skunks work the lawns of the Stroudsburg suburbs
Monroe County.absent_or_rare: black bears are abundant in the Poconos and are the county's biggest wildlife presence, but they are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed and never a private removal booking — the same goes for deer, beavers, and porcupines in the deep woods

Centre County.region: central Pennsylvania, Penn State country in the ridge-and-valley heart of the state
Centre County.nearest_metro: State College is the regional center, about 85 miles northwest of Harrisburg
natural_features: Spring Creek and Bald Eagle Creek corridors
Rothrock and Bald Eagle state forests
Penns Creek and Penn's Cave country to the east
Centre County.habitat_type: a university town and suburbs in Happy Valley, historic Bellefonte, and long farm valleys between forested ridges
Centre County.regional_wildlife: squirrels and raccoons run the student-rental and older housing of State College and Bellefonte, groundhogs burrow the farm valleys of Penns and Nittany, and bats roost in Victorian Bellefonte and farmhouses along Spring Creek
Centre County.absent_or_rare: black bears, deer, and bobcats fill the surrounding state forests but are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed rather than household removal work

Blair County.region: central Pennsylvania in the Allegheny Front country around Altoona
Blair County.nearest_metro: Altoona is the regional center, about 95 miles east of Pittsburgh
natural_features: Brush Mountain and the Allegheny Front
Juniata River and Frankstown Branch corridor
Horseshoe Curve and the railroad corridor
Blair County.habitat_type: the railroad city of Altoona in its mountain bowl, older boroughs, and farm valleys along the Juniata
Blair County.regional_wildlife: raccoons, squirrels, and rats persist in Altoona's dense older housing, bats colonize churches and mill-era attics in Hollidaysburg and Tyrone, and groundhogs and skunks work the valley farms and suburban edges
Blair County.absent_or_rare: black bears come off Brush Mountain regularly but are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed, as are deer and beavers along the Juniata

Cambria County.region: west-central Pennsylvania on the Allegheny Plateau around Johnstown
Cambria County.nearest_metro: Johnstown is the regional center, about 65 miles east of Pittsburgh
natural_features: Conemaugh River gorge and the Johnstown floodplain
Prince Gallitzin State Park and Glendale Lake
Cambria County.habitat_type: the steep industrial city of Johnstown, coal and steel boroughs on the plateau, and forested ridges
Cambria County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and rats work Johnstown's dense hillside housing and older commercial blocks, bats roost in plateau churches and Ebensburg's older homes, and skunks and groundhogs fill the borough edges from Portage to Nanty Glo
Cambria County.absent_or_rare: black bears, deer, and fishers are common on the plateau but are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed rather than private removal work

Lycoming County.region: north-central Pennsylvania on the West Branch Susquehanna River, the largest county in the state by land area
Lycoming County.nearest_metro: Williamsport is the regional center, about 85 miles north of Harrisburg
natural_features: Loyalsock Creek and Loyalsock State Forest
Pine Creek and the Pennsylvania Grand Canyon western edge
Lycoming County.habitat_type: the river city of Williamsport, lumber-era boroughs, and a vast forested interior in the Loyalsock
Lycoming County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and squirrels fill Williamsport's lumber-era housing, bats roost in river-town churches and older homes from Muncy to Jersey Shore, and groundhogs and skunks work the farm valley along the West Branch
Lycoming County.absent_or_rare: black bears, deer, bobcats, and fishers are abundant in the Loyalsock State Forest but are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed, never routine removal calls

Allegheny County.region: southwestern Pennsylvania at the forks of the Ohio, where the Allegheny and Monongahela rivers meet
Allegheny County.nearest_metro: Pittsburgh is the regional metro center
natural_features: Allegheny, Monongahela, and Ohio river corridors
Frick Park and Schenley Park woodlands
Youghiogheny River at the county's southeast
Allegheny County.habitat_type: dense urban Pittsburgh neighborhoods on steep river hills, streetcar suburbs, and Mon Valley mill towns
Allegheny County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats and raccoons run Pittsburgh's older rowhouse and hillside neighborhoods and the Mon Valley mill towns, gray squirrels are relentless in the streetcar suburbs from Mount Lebanon to Penn Hills, and groundhogs burrow the river hillsides and park edges countywide
Allegheny County.absent_or_rare: white-tailed deer are heavily overabundant in the parks and suburbs but are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed, and beavers, foxes, and coyotes along the rivers are not routine household removal work

Westmoreland County.region: southwestern Pennsylvania in the Laurel Highlands foothills east of Pittsburgh
natural_features: Loyalhanna Creek and Keystone State Park
Linn Run and Forbes State Forest edge
Westmoreland County.habitat_type: Greensburg and older industrial boroughs, Pittsburgh commuter suburbs in the west, and mountain country on Chestnut Ridge
Westmoreland County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and squirrels fill Greensburg, Latrobe, and the western suburbs, groundhogs burrow farms and big lots under Chestnut Ridge, and rats persist in the older Mon Valley and New Kensington blocks
Westmoreland County.absent_or_rare: black bears are regular on Chestnut Ridge and in the Forbes State Forest but are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed, as are deer and beavers on the Loyalhanna

Washington County.region: southwestern Pennsylvania in the Marcellus gas country south of Pittsburgh
Washington County.habitat_type: the older city of Washington, Mon Valley river towns, gas-country rural land, and affluent Peters Township suburbs
Washington County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs burrow farm, gas-pad, and big-lot edges across the county, raccoons and squirrels fill Washington, Canonsburg, and McMurray housing, and skunks work the Mon Valley river towns at dusk
Washington County.absent_or_rare: black bears are occasional visitors in the southern townships, and deer, beavers, and muskrats along the Monongahela and Chartiers Creek are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed

Butler County.region: western Pennsylvania north of Pittsburgh, mixing Cranberry suburbs with farm and gas country
Butler County.nearest_metro: Pittsburgh (about 30 miles south of Butler city)
natural_features: Moraine State Park and Lake Arthur
Allegheny River at the county's east
Butler County.habitat_type: fast-growing Cranberry suburbs in the south, the older city of Butler, and rural farm and woodland in the north
Butler County.regional_wildlife: squirrels and raccoons run the new Cranberry and Mars subdivisions as their trees mature, groundhogs and moles work the farm and big-lot north, and bats roost in Butler city's older housing and Slippery Rock borough homes
Butler County.absent_or_rare: black bears wander the northern woods but are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed, as are deer and beavers on Lake Arthur and the Connoquenessing

Beaver County.region: western Pennsylvania along the Ohio River northwest of Pittsburgh
Beaver County.habitat_type: historic Ohio River boroughs, steel-era towns along the Beaver River, and suburban growth in the center
Beaver County.regional_wildlife: raccoons, squirrels, and rats persist in the river towns from Ambridge to Beaver Falls, groundhogs burrow the hillsides above the Ohio, and bats roost in the Victorian housing of Beaver and Rochester
Beaver County.absent_or_rare: white-tailed deer and beavers along the rivers and in Raccoon Creek State Park are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed rather than routine removal work

Mercer County.region: western Pennsylvania on the Ohio line, in the Shenango River valley
Mercer County.nearest_metro: Youngstown, Ohio (about 15 miles west of Sharon)
natural_features: Shenango River and Shenango River Lake
Lake Wilhelm and Maurice K. Goddard State Park
Mercer County.habitat_type: small steel-era cities in the Shenango valley, Grove City's outlet-corridor growth, and farm and lake country
Mercer County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and squirrels fill Sharon, Farrell, and Hermitage housing, groundhogs burrow farm edges from Grove City to Greenville, and bats roost in the valley's older churches and homes
Mercer County.absent_or_rare: black bears are occasional in the northern woods, and deer, beavers, and muskrats around Shenango Lake and Pymatuning are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed

Fayette County.region: southwestern Pennsylvania in the Laurel Highlands along the West Virginia line
natural_features: Youghiogheny River and Ohiopyle State Park
Fort Necessity and the National Road corridor
Fayette County.habitat_type: the mountain city of Uniontown, river and rail boroughs, coal country, and Laurel Highlands resort land
Fayette County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats work Uniontown and Connellsville housing and the mountain cabins around Ohiopyle, skunks and groundhogs fill the valley farms, and rats persist in the older Monongahela riverfront blocks of Brownsville
Fayette County.absent_or_rare: black bears are common in the Laurel Highlands but are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed, as are deer, beavers, and fishers in the state parks

Erie County.region: northwestern Pennsylvania on Lake Erie, the state's only Great Lakes shoreline county
Erie County.nearest_metro: Erie is the regional center, about 100 miles from both Pittsburgh and Buffalo
natural_features: Lake Erie shoreline and Presque Isle State Park
Walnut Creek and Elk Creek steelhead corridors
Erie County.habitat_type: the older lake city of Erie, grape-belt boroughs along the shore, and Edinboro lake country inland
Erie County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats and raccoons run Erie's older east- and west-side neighborhoods and waterfront, groundhogs burrow the grape-belt farms from North East to Girard, and bats roost in lake-effect country homes and Edinboro cottages
Erie County.absent_or_rare: white-tailed deer on Presque Isle and beavers and muskrats in the lake marshes are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed, and black bears are only occasional visitors inland

Armstrong County.region: western Pennsylvania along the Allegheny River northeast of Pittsburgh
Armstrong County.habitat_type: river boroughs and rural farm and woodland
Armstrong County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and squirrels fill Kittanning and Ford City housing, groundhogs burrow the farm country, and bats roost in river-town churches
Armstrong County.absent_or_rare: black bears, deer, and beavers along the Allegheny are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed rather than routine removal work

Bedford County.region: south-central Pennsylvania in the Allegheny foothills along the Maryland line
Bedford County.habitat_type: historic Bedford borough, farm valleys, and mountain forest
Bedford County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs and skunks work the farm valleys, raccoons den in Bedford and Everett homes, and bats use the older stone housing
Bedford County.absent_or_rare: black bears and deer are abundant in the mountains but Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed

Bradford County.region: northern-tier Pennsylvania along the Susquehanna River and the New York line
Bradford County.nearest_metro: Elmira, New York (about 20 miles north of Sayre)
Bradford County.habitat_type: river boroughs and dairy farm country in the Endless Mountains foothills
Bradford County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs burrow dairy farm edges, raccoons and bats fill Towanda and Sayre housing, and skunks work the valley farms
Bradford County.absent_or_rare: black bears, deer, and beavers are common but Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed

Cameron County.region: north-central Pennsylvania in the Pennsylvania Wilds, one of the state's least populous counties
Cameron County.nearest_metro: St. Marys in Elk County (about 15 miles west)
natural_features: Sinnemahoning Creek and Sinnemahoning State Park
Cameron County.habitat_type: deep forest and small creek-valley communities
Cameron County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats are the house calls in Emporium, skunks work camp properties, and porcupines gnaw outbuildings through the forest
Cameron County.absent_or_rare: elk, black bears, deer, and bobcats define this county and are entirely Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed

Carbon County.region: eastern Pennsylvania in the Pocono foothills along the Lehigh River
natural_features: Lehigh River gorge and Lehigh Gorge State Park
Carbon County.habitat_type: historic Jim Thorpe, coal boroughs, and vacation and lake communities
Carbon County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats fill Jim Thorpe and Lehighton housing and lake homes around Beltzville, and skunks work the borough edges
Carbon County.absent_or_rare: black bears are common in the gorge country but Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed

Clarion County.region: western Pennsylvania along the Allegheny River and the Clarion River
natural_features: Cook Forest State Park southern edge
Clarion County.habitat_type: college borough of Clarion, river towns, and farm and forest land
Clarion County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs burrow the farm country, raccoons and bats fill Clarion and river-town homes, and skunks work the borough edges
Clarion County.absent_or_rare: black bears, deer, and beavers along the Clarion River are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed

Clearfield County.region: central Pennsylvania on the Allegheny Plateau along the West Branch Susquehanna
Clearfield County.nearest_metro: State College (about 40 miles southeast of Clearfield)
Clearfield County.habitat_type: plateau boroughs, DuBois as the commercial hub, and extensive forest
Clearfield County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats fill Clearfield and DuBois housing, skunks and groundhogs work the plateau farms and camp properties
Clearfield County.absent_or_rare: black bears, deer, and elk at the county's east are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed

Clinton County.region: central Pennsylvania on the West Branch Susquehanna at the Bald Eagle valley
Clinton County.habitat_type: the river city of Lock Haven, valley boroughs, and mountain forest
Clinton County.regional_wildlife: raccoons, squirrels, and bats fill Lock Haven and Mill Hall housing, and groundhogs work the Bald Eagle valley farms
Clinton County.absent_or_rare: black bears, deer, and bobcats in the mountain forest are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed

Columbia County.region: central Pennsylvania on the Susquehanna River's north branch
natural_features: Ricketts Glen State Park southern edge
Columbia County.habitat_type: the university borough of Bloomsburg, Berwick's industrial blocks, and farm country
Columbia County.regional_wildlife: squirrels and raccoons run Bloomsburg and Berwick housing, groundhogs burrow the farm country, and bats roost in older river-town homes
Columbia County.absent_or_rare: black bears come down from the northern mountains but are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed

Crawford County.region: northwestern Pennsylvania around Pymatuning Reservoir and Conneaut Lake
natural_features: Pymatuning Reservoir and Pymatuning State Park
Crawford County.habitat_type: Meadville and Titusville small cities, lake communities, and dairy farm country
Crawford County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs and moles work the farm and lake lawns, raccoons and bats fill Meadville and Titusville homes, and skunks den around Conneaut Lake cottages
Crawford County.absent_or_rare: deer, beavers, and muskrats at Pymatuning are Pennsylvania Game Commission-managed, and black bears are occasional in the woods

Elk County.region: north-central Pennsylvania in the Pennsylvania Wilds elk country
natural_features: Elk Country Visitor Center and Winslow Hill near Benezette
Elk County.habitat_type: small industrial boroughs in deep forest, famous for its wild elk herd
